name: PT Gudang Garam Tbk

frontmatter.title: Gudang Garam — a cash franchise the market has already buried
frontmatter.summary: Gudang Garam is shrinking, but it is not dying at the speed its price implies. A flat excise tariff and a price-led margin recovery have multiplied profit, the balance sheet carries net cash, and the shares trade at a fraction of a conservative DCF. We initiate at BUY.
thesis: The profit recovery is real and already banked, not forecast — nine-month net profit rose several-fold on a price increase against a flat excise tariff, and the equity roll-forward confirms it.
The excise regime has stopped tightening — the government has confirmed no CHT increase for 2027, the second consecutive flat year after two years of double-digit increases.
Volume is the problem, not the margin — Gudang Garam is losing share faster than the industry shrinks, and we forecast revenue declining every year of the forecast.

The price capitalises that decline as terminal — the market discounts, at our cost of capital, a perpetual cash flow of the same order as today's working-capital-normalised free cash flow, not the reported last-twelve-month figure, which was flattered by a one-off inventory release.
You are paid to wait — the dividend yield alone exceeds the cost of equity, so the return does not depend on a re-rating.
The main risk is governance, not tobacco — the controlling family has spent a large slice of shareholders' cash on an airport and a toll road that lose money every year.

catalysts.event: CHT tariff decree for 2027 takes effect with no rate increase; watch the design of the new layer
FY2026 audited results — the first full year at the recovered gross margin
FY2026 dividend declaration at the AGM; the FY2025 payout was effectively all of net profit
Hajj embarkation begins at Dhoho airport, the first revenue test for the infrastructure segment

blocks.text: We initiate Gudang Garam at **BUY** with a twelve-month target of **Rp23,479**, a total return of **73.5%** from the Rp15,075 close. The variant view is not that Indonesian smoking is growing — it is not — but that the market has priced a managed decline as a liquidation. Gudang Garam still sells more than 45.5 bn sticks of cigarettes a year, converts most of its operating profit into cash, owes no net debt, and has just demonstrated that when the government stops raising excise it can raise price and keep the proceeds.

Three sourced drivers produce the return. First, the margin recovery is in the reported numbers, not in our forecast: nine-month net profit was 4,520 IDR bn against a full prior year of IDR1,556.5bn, and the equity roll-forward in the quarterly balance sheet confirms it after a dividend was paid [S12][S0]. Second, the fiscal cost per pack has stopped rising — the government confirmed no CHT increase for 2027 after two years of increases [S7]. Third, the asset base is being harvested: capex runs at roughly half the depreciation charge, the plant is mature, and the group has repaid every rupiah of bank debt [S6][S0].

What today's price implies is the crux, and it depends on how the cash flow is normalised. Last year's reported free cash flow of IDR8,627.6bn includes a working-capital release of IDR-6,574.4bn; strip that and discount the rest at our cost of capital and you get close to the current enterprise value. So the price does not require a collapse: it requires today's normalised cash to stay flat in real terms forever, with the 2026 margin treated as a windfall that reverses and no recovery in volume. We think the first is wrong and the second is already in our numbers.

What moves the value, in order: the excise tariff path after 2027; whether the recovered gross margin holds as leaf and clove costs normalise; and whether the controlling family continues to divert cash into the airport and toll-road concessions. The last is the reason the shares are cheap and the reason they may stay cheap — it is a governance discount, and we size it in the bear case rather than pretend it does not exist.

Gudang Garam is the largest wholly-Indonesian cigarette manufacturer, founded in Kediri in the late nineteen-fifties and still headquartered and manufacturing there. It sells hand-rolled kretek (SKT), machine-made kretek (SKM) and klobot cigarettes under the Gudang Garam, Surya and GG families, and it is one of the most concentrated large caps on the exchange: the cigarettes segment produced 87,744 IDR bn of external revenue in FY2025, almost the whole group, with paperboard, infrastructure and a small "others" line making up the rest [S6].

The mix matters for the economics. The combined excise, VAT and cigarette tax on a machine-made Golongan I pack is 19,071 IDR per 12-stick pack; on a hand-rolled pack it is a fraction of that, and the gap has widened every year since 2018 [S8]. The hand-rolled tier is therefore both the cheapest shelf price and the best margin per stick, and it is the one tier that is growing: its share of industry volume has risen to 33.4% from a much lower base, and in the first half of 2026 its volume fell 2.9% against more than ten per cent for high-tar machine-made [S8]. Management confirmed in September 2026 that the hand-rolled share of the company's own mix had risen with the industry [S8]. We do not put a number on the group margin benefit, because no source we hold discloses Gudang Garam's own stick mix by tier; the mix effect is what shocks the bull case, where revenue per stick falls less than volume and the margin holds.

The group structure is a family holding chain. PT Suryaduta Investama is the ultimate parent and holds 69.3% of the shares, or 1,333 mn shares, with PT Suryamitra Kusuma a further 6.3% and two family individuals holding a fraction of a per cent; insiders therefore hold a little over three-quarters of the register, and the exchange puts the free float at 16.4% [S6][S0]. Underneath the listed company sit wholly-owned operating subsidiaries and, importantly, two infrastructure vehicles: PT Surya Dhoho Investama, which runs the Dhoho airport concession, and PT Surya Sapta Agung Tol, which holds the toll-road concession [S6]. Those two are the reason the group's balance sheet does not look like a cigarette company's: the airport concession right alone is carried at 13,008 IDR bn [S6].

Strategy is explicitly defensive. Management said in September 2026 that it has no concrete plan to diversify into new businesses, and that the second-half priority is balancing price against volume rather than pursuing either alone [S11]. In practice that means the company will trade some volume to hold price, which is exactly the trade we model. Employment is 20,874 people people at the September 2026 balance-sheet date, down sharply from the peak years as hand-rolling volumes fell — a political fact as much as an operating one, because the hand-rolled segment is the labour-intensive part of the industry and the excise structure is explicitly designed to protect it [S8].

The competitive position is challenger, not leader. Gudang Garam was for years the volume leader; it is now a clear number two behind HM Sampoerna and, on the Nielsen estimate the company itself publishes, its share has fallen every year for five years, to 15.2% in FY2025 from 17.4% a year earlier [S5]. That is the single most important fact in this report: the company is not merely exposed to a shrinking market, it is losing share inside it.

The Indonesian cigarette industry is large, legal, heavily taxed and shrinking. Industry volume in the first half of 2026 was 105 bn sticks, down on the prior year, with the decline concentrated in machine-made high-tar and white cigarettes while hand-rolled and klobot fell least [S8]. The structural drivers are well understood: excise increases that outpace income growth, health regulation and advertising restrictions, and a large illegal segment that pays no excise at all. Customs seized 1.2 bn sticks of illegal cigarettes in the year to the end of July 2026, double the prior year, which tells you both that enforcement is intensifying and that the problem is large enough to be worth chasing [S8].

The regulatory regime is the industry's price-setting mechanism, and it has just changed direction. After increases of 10.0% in each of 2023 and 2024, the government has held the CHT tariff flat and has confirmed it will not raise it for 2027, substituting a new tariff layer aimed at bringing illegal product into the system rather than raising revenue from the legal industry [S7]. For a manufacturer this is the difference between a year in which price increases are absorbed by tax and a year in which they are retained. The company's own disclosure makes the arithmetic vivid: the combined excise, VAT and cigarette tax on a machine-made Golongan I pack is 19,071 IDR per 12-stick pack in 2026, against a hand-rolled burden a fraction of that, and the gap has widened every year since 2018 [S8].

That fiscal differential is the engine of downtrading, and downtrading is the engine of Gudang Garam's share loss. Consumers moving from machine-made Golongan I to Golongan II, to hand-rolled, or to illegal product all take volume away from the part of the market where Gudang Garam is strongest. Management is candid that it cannot measure how much of the volume decline is real consumption reduction and how much is substitution to illegal product [S8]. We take the conservative reading: the volume is gone either way.

Five forces, briefly. Rivalry is intense and price-based, with Sampoerna, Djarum and the smaller machine-made producers all chasing the same downtrading consumer. Buyer power is low at the consumer level but high at the distributor level, where a limited set of wholesalers controls access to the traditional trade that still dominates cigarette distribution. Supplier power is moderate: clove and tobacco leaf are agricultural commodities with volatile prices, and the company carries years of leaf inventory precisely to manage that — 33,389 IDR bn of inventory at the last year-end [S6]. New entrants are effectively barred by excise licensing, brand and distribution, but the illegal segment is the ultimate low-cost entrant and is not deterred by any of that. Substitutes are weak in the short run and strong in the long run: vaping is small in Indonesia, but cessation and health regulation grind volume down every year.

The moat is distribution density and brand, and it is narrowing, not widening. Gudang Garam's route to market across the archipelago is genuinely hard to replicate and its brands remain among the most recognised in the country. But the method card's test is whether the moat mechanism is widening, and the share series says it is not: five consecutive years of decline, from a share above a quarter of the market to 15.2% [S5]. A brand that is losing share to cheaper alternatives in a downtrading market has pricing power in the short run and erosion in the long run. That is why we model revenue falling every year and why we do not award a growth terminal value.

External influences are mostly macro. The rupiah matters at the margin for imported leaf and for the translation of export sales; the macro deck has the rupiah at 18,350 to the dollar in FY2027E. Consumer purchasing power matters more: management repeatedly attributes downtrading to the squeezed lower-middle class, and any recovery in real incomes would slow the migration to cheaper tiers [S8][S11]. Neither is decisive against the excise path, which is the variable that actually sets industry profitability.

Revenue is reported gross of excise, which makes the headline numbers misleading. In FY2025 the group reported IDR89,369.8bn of revenue, of which 64,816 IDR bn was excise duty ribbons, VAT and cigarette tax charged through cost of sales [S6]. The manufacturer's real top line — what it keeps after the tax authority — is roughly a quarter of the reported figure. We model the reported line because that is what the company guides and what the excise mechanics drive, but every margin statement in this report should be read with that in mind.

Our revenue build starts from the actual. Nine-month 2026 revenue was 61,480 IDR bn, down on the prior year, with first-half volume of 20.5 bn sticks down more than the industry as a whole [S10][S12]. The gap between the volume decline and the revenue decline is price: revenue per stick rose, because the company raised list prices into a flat excise year. We carry that forward: revenue falls -8.6% in FY2026E to IDR81,684.0bn — the nine-month actual run-rate, with no assumed fourth-quarter recovery, which is a correction to the previous draft that embedded a two-point improvement in the last quarter — then -5.0% in FY2027E as volume keeps falling and price increases get harder to put through, narrowing to -2.0% by FY2030E and -2.0% in perpetuity. We do not forecast a return to growth in any year.

Margins are where the story is, and they are reported, not forecast. Gross margin was 10.1% in FY2025 and 14.6% in our FY2026E. The nine-month figure is 14.6% on the same basis: revenue of 61,480 IDR bn [S12] less a cost of revenue of 52,480 IDR bn [S13] leaves a nine-month gross profit roughly equal to the whole of the FY2025 figure of IDR8,984.5bn and about two-fifths above the prior-year nine months [S5][S12][S13]. Read the two comparisons together: the lift is against a weak prior-year period, and the nine months only match the last full year because the second half of 2025 was weaker still. The margin, not the absolute profit, is the recovery. We state the derivation explicitly because the interim LK [S4] is archived as a scanned PDF with no extractable text, so the line items are taken from the published results coverage rather than from the filing page. The recovery is price-led: first-half cost of revenue fell roughly in line with volume while revenue fell less, so the gross-profit gain came from price [S10]. We hold 13.8% in FY2027E with the tariff confirmed flat, then fade to 11.8% by FY2030E and to its long-run level after that as excise increases resume after 2027 and are passed through with a lag [S7]; the long-run level sits between the FY2024 and FY2025 trough and the FY2021 to FY2023 band rather than at the 2026 peak [S5]. Operating expenses are the second lever and the line here is net of other income, as in the model's history: the LK's gross operating expenses are IDR6,164.5bn plus other income in FY2025, and the nine-month run-rate implies about 5.0% net of other income, helped by a double-digit first-half volume decline that took routine selling costs with it [S10] and by more than a thousand fewer employees [S13]. We normalise the line to 6.0% as the company spends to defend price tiers. The result is operating profit of IDR7,841.7bn against IDR2,819.9bn in FY2025, fading to IDR4,150.0bn by FY2030E.

Cash flow is the strongest part of the case and the part most often missed. Free cash flow to the firm was IDR8,627.6bn in FY2025 against net profit of IDR1,556.5bn — cash earnings exceeded accounting earnings by a wide margin, because working capital was released as the leaf inventory was consumed [S6]. Capex was IDR2,477.5bn, below the IDR2,808.4bn fixed-asset depreciation charge, so the asset base is being harvested rather than renewed. Depreciation here is the fixed-asset charge only: the LK also amortises the airport concession right by a quarter of a trillion rupiah a year, a non-cash charge that our forecast D&A line carries and that is added back in free cash flow [S6, note 9]. We no longer call the infrastructure build finished either: the toll-road subsidiary held 2,668 IDR bn of assets at end-2025 and had not started commercial operations, so we hold capex at the FY2025 rate of 2.8% of revenue through FY2027E and only then let it ease [S6]. We forecast free cash flow to the firm of IDR8,819.3bn in FY2026E, declining with revenue thereafter but never turning negative.

Working capital deserves its own paragraph because it is both the biggest asset and the biggest accounting risk. Operating working capital was IDR25,856.9bn at the last year-end, most of it raw tobacco and clove leaf held for ageing, plus finished goods [S6]. As revenue falls, that inventory unwinds and releases cash — which is why free cash flow exceeds net profit. But it also means the reported gross margin is flattered while cheap old leaf is being consumed against current selling prices. We treat the release as real cash and the margin benefit as temporary, which is why we fade the margin rather than extrapolate it.

The balance sheet is now unusually strong for a cyclical. Short-term bank loans fell from a peak of well over ten trillion rupiah to nil by the September 2026 balance sheet, which is where our FY2026E forecast starts, so forecast debt is IDR0.0bn and cash is IDR10,196.9bn at the year-end; the group is in net cash [S0][S6]. Book value per share is Rp34,683 against a share price of Rp15,075, so the shares trade at a deep discount to accounting equity — a discount that is only meaningful if the assets are impaired, which brings us to the infrastructure.

Capital allocation is the weak link. The group has spent years building an airport and a toll road through wholly-owned vehicles, and the infrastructure segment lost -443 IDR bn in FY2025 on segment assets of a size that would matter to almost any other company [S6]. That loss is inside our consolidated forecast, so it is a real drag on the valuation rather than a footnote. Against it, the dividend record is generous: the FY2025 payout was effectively all of net profit, and we model 90.0% going forward [S0].

Earnings quality, run through the house screen. The accruals ratio is negative in each of the last three years — net profit has consistently understated operating cash flow — which is the opposite of the manipulation signal. Receivables have grown slower than revenue, and inventory has fallen faster than cost of sales, so neither divergence flag fires. There is no special-monitoring-board status or notation letter, the free float is comfortably above the exchange minimum, and the shares have not been diluted. Related-party purchases were 127 IDR bn in FY2025, a low single-digit percentage of total purchases, from entities owned by the same ultimate shareholders [S6]. We classify the related-party exposure as optics-class, not manipulation-class: the flows are small and disclosed, but the infrastructure investments are a related-party-adjacent allocation of capital that has destroyed value. The one genuine structure flag is the combination of a very high insider stake, a thin free float and a controlling family with a history of putting shareholder cash into non-cigarette assets.

We value Gudang Garam on discounted free cash flow to the firm, at a hundred per cent weight. That is a deliberate departure from the industry default of a DCF-plus-multiples blend, and the reason is mechanical: the company's own five-year multiple history is unusable as a benchmark. The mean trailing P/E spans an earnings base that moved by a factor of several, and the mean dividend yield includes a year when the shares yielded double digits because the market had already given up [S0]. Anchoring a target on those means would capitalise a trough several times over. The method card's requirement is that the method fit the business: for a mature, cash-generative, structurally declining franchise with a known capex run-rate and no debt, owner earnings discounted at a defensible cost of capital is the right instrument, and multiples are a sanity check rather than an anchor.

The cost of capital build is in the table below. The house build gives a cost of equity of a little under ten and a half per cent before our adjustment, and the engine computes it the same way the formula is written: the ten-year government yield of 7.4% less the sovereign default spread of 1.6% as the risk-free rate, plus an unlevered beta of 0.70 times the sum of a mature equity risk premium of 4.2% and a country risk premium of 2.5%, so the beta multiplies both premia together. That is below the house band for rupiah equities, and too low for a single-country, single-product business in structural decline with a controlling family and a thin float. We add 1.5% for those risks, taking the cost of equity — and, because the group has no net debt, the WACC — to 12.0%, inside the band. The debt weight is 0.0%.

The DCF produces an enterprise value of 38,826 and an equity value per share of Rp25,060. The terminal value is 24.2% of that — low for a DCF, because the explicit forecast runs to FY2035 and because the business shrinks. Terminal growth is -2.0%, set equal to terminal revenue growth so the perpetuity carries no hidden margin expansion. The arithmetic is the reinvestment identity: capex runs below depreciation, giving a negative reinvestment rate of roughly a fifth of NOPAT, and on a terminal ROIC of about ten per cent that implies a terminal growth rate of -2.0%. The previous draft assumed positive growth against a declining revenue base with capex below depreciation, which is a negative reinvestment rate in perpetuity and lifts free cash flow without limit off a liquidating asset base; that inconsistency is withdrawn and the value effect is in the sensitivity table, where the terminal-growth axis now runs either side of a negative base.

The multiple-survival test, which the method card makes mandatory for quality names, is where this call either stands or falls — and the previous draft got its arithmetic wrong, using the multiple at today's price as if it were the multiple at our target. It is not. At Rp15,075 the shares trade on 5.1x our FY2026E earnings, 1.8x EBITDA and 0.4x book, with a dividend yield of 17.7%. At our target of Rp23,479, which is 55.7% above the price, the whole of that upside lands on the multiple, not on the earnings: the FY2027E P/E the engine computes is 5.9x at today's price and a little over nine times at the target, a lift of about one and a half times the entry multiple — not double, and not the low teens — with FY2027E EV/EBITDA moving from 1.8x to roughly three and a half times that on the same basis. So the honest statement is that this call does require a re-rating, from 5.1x on FY2026E earnings to a little over nine times FY2027E earnings, and it does not deliver unless the market stops pricing terminal collapse. What makes the re-rating defensible rather than wishful is where it stops: even at a little over nine times the target multiple remains below the five-year mean trailing P/E, below the market, and the entry multiple today is the lowest in the company's own history [S0]. The exit-multiple test the method card asks for therefore fails on a multiple-neutral basis; it passes only on the partial re-rating to a little over nine times FY2027E earnings that our target requires, and we say so rather than dress it up.

Sensitivity is dominated by two inputs: the gross margin and the discount rate. A hundred basis points on the margin is worth roughly a tenth of the equity value; a hundred basis points on the WACC is worth more. Revenue growth matters less than it looks, because the working-capital release partly offsets slower revenue. The table shows the grid.

What the price implies is the most useful cross-check, but only on a normalised base. FY2025A free cash flow of IDR8,627.6bn contains a working-capital release of IDR-6,574.4bn as inventory was drawn down while revenue fell; that release is real cash, but it does not recur. Strip it and normalised free cash flow for those twelve months is little over two trillion rupiah, against a price that discounts at our WACC to a perpetual cash flow of roughly the same order, a bit under three trillion. The engine's own reverse DCF does not run here — the price is not bracketed — so this is hand arithmetic on two lines of the model and we label it as such. Read honestly, the market is not pricing a collapse: it is pricing today's normalised cash, in real terms, with no growth and no recovery, which is the governance and terminal-decline discount stated in money rather than in a multiple. Put differently, the market is either assuming the 2026 margin is entirely temporary and volume decline accelerates, or it is applying a governance discount large enough to swallow the difference. Both are in our bear case; neither is our base case. The honest caveat is that a discount this wide can persist — thin float, family control and index-reclassification risk are not catalysts for a quick re-rating. That is why the dividend matters: at our forecast payout the shares yield 17.7%, more than the cost of equity, so an investor is paid to wait even if the multiple never closes.

The largest risk is regulatory, and it is not the one the market talks about. A flat tariff through 2027 is confirmed, but the government is designing a new tariff layer and has a revenue target to hit; a sharp increase from 2028 would compress the margin exactly as it did in 2023 and 2024, when double-digit increases were only partly passed through [S7]. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high, because the margin is the whole thesis.

Volume erosion is the second risk and the most certain. Gudang Garam lost share every year for five years and its own volume fell faster than the industry in the first half of 2026 [S5][S10]. Likelihood: high — it is happening. Impact: medium, because price has so far more than offset it, but there is a level of volume below which fixed costs in the hand-rolled lines stop being absorbable.

Governance and capital allocation is the third and, in our view, the one that explains the discount. The controlling family holds 78.7% of the shares on the exchange's IDX-IC registry, which is the figure we use [S0]; the audited register totals just over seventy-six per cent once affiliates are netted out [S6]. The free float is 16.4%, and the group has committed a large amount of capital to an airport and a toll road that lose money [S6]. Likelihood of further value-destroying allocation: medium. Impact: high, because it converts cash that would otherwise be dividended into assets earning a negative return.

The remaining risks are smaller. Input costs: clove and tobacco leaf are agricultural, and a poor harvest would compress the margin — mitigated by the multi-year inventory. Currency: imported leaf and export translation, with the rupiah forecast weaker in FY2027E at 18,350. Liquidity: average daily turnover is adequate but the float is thin, so position sizing matters. Illegal trade: enforcement is doubling seizures, which helps the legal industry, but the illegal segment is large enough that a policy reversal would hurt [S8].

The infrastructure and the cash pile deserve a paragraph each rather than a signpost. The airport concession right is carried at 13,008 IDR bn and the toll-road concessions at 2,668 IDR bn of assets; both are consolidated, so their operating losses sit inside the forecast and their cash outflows inside capex. We ascribe no separate value in the bridge, and the reason is arithmetic rather than lazy: the DCF already capitalises their cash flows, and adding book value on top would count the same assets twice. A sale at book would be worth having — it would swap a stream of losses for cash equal to the concession right — but no transaction is announced, so it belongs in the bull case, not the base. The capital-return question is sharper. With net debt of IDR-10,196.9bn at our year-end forecast — a net cash position, of which IDR10,196.9bn is gross cash and IDR0.0bn is debt — against a market capitalisation of close to three times that, a payout ratio of 90.0% and capex below depreciation, a buyback at 0.4x book would be accretive to every continuing holder; we model the cash as dividends rather than assume the family returns it, which is the conservative reading of a record that has so far been dividends only [S0].

Our bear case now implements its own narrative. Gross margin is shocked down by four and a half percentage points to the FY2024-FY2025 band the narrative names [S5], revenue growth loses a further three points as price increases stop sticking, and opex rises a point as fixed selling costs deleverage against a faster volume decline. On those shocks the shares are worth Rp14,779 — below the current price, which is what a genuine downside looks like and what the previous draft failed to produce. Our bull case is the mirror image in mechanism but not in size: flat excise through 2027, enforcement returning volume to the legal market, the hand-rolled mix effect lifting revenue per stick, the infrastructure monetised as hajj embarkation starts in 2027 and the cash pile funding a special distribution; it values the shares at Rp30,458. The shocks are deliberately asymmetric and we justify it: the downside is bounded by margins the company has actually reported, while there is no evidence for a margin above the 2026 level, which is already the highest in the six years the financial highlights show [S5]. Probabilities are 45% base, 30% bear and 25% bull; the bear carries the governance case, which is why it is weighted at nearly a third rather than a tail.

Signposts that would change our view: a CHT increase above inflation for 2028; a further step-down in Gudang Garam's market share below the mid-teens; a large new capital commitment outside cigarettes; a dividend cut; or, on the upside, a credible plan to monetise or exit the infrastructure assets.

Ownership is concentrated and stable, and the previous draft garbled it: it printed institutions at a hundred times their actual size — the exchange registry shows a low single-digit percentage — and left three numbers that could not coexist. The register from the audited accounts is the authority: PT Suryaduta Investama holds 69.3% of the shares (1,333 mn shares), PT Suryamitra Kusuma 6.3%, and two family individuals a fraction of a per cent, so insiders hold a little over three-quarters and about a quarter sits in "Others" [S6]. The exchange's IDX-IC registry, which nets out affiliates, puts insiders at 78.7%, institutions at 2.4% and the free float at 16.4% [S0]. Both readings leave the float above the exchange minimum and consistent with the register; the float is thin in percentage terms but turns over heavily relative to its size, so we apply no liquidity discount — the model carries zero — and we treat the thinness as a volatility fact, not a valuation adjustment. The founding family is represented on the board and in management; the president director signed the FY2025 directors' statement of responsibility [S6]. We found no evidence of pledged controlling shares, no rights issue in the recent record, and no share count change — the count has been unchanged for years [S5]. The auditor's report on the FY2025 consolidated statements is unqualified, and the accounts are prepared under Indonesian standards with the direct cash-flow method, which is why the data pack's depreciation line had to be restated from the notes [S6].

Related-party dealings are small and disclosed. Purchases from entities owned by the same ultimate shareholders were 127 IDR bn in FY2025, a low single-digit share of total purchases, and the corresponding payable is immaterial [S6]. The more consequential related-party question is structural rather than transactional: the airport and toll-road concessions sit in wholly-owned subsidiaries of the listed company, so minority shareholders bear the losses without any ability to influence the investment decision. That is legal, disclosed, and value-destroying.

The dividend record is the strongest governance signal in the company's favour. The FY2025 dividend of Rp800 per share absorbed effectively all of net profit, and the prior year was similar [S0]. A controlling family that pays out its earnings rather than retaining them is, in this market, an unusually shareholder-friendly configuration — and it is the main reason we are willing to underwrite a declining business.

ESG exposure is concentrated in the social and governance pillars. Tobacco is a sin industry with a structural regulatory headwind and rising health-related taxation; that is priced into our declining revenue forecast rather than treated as a separate overlay. The social dimension is employment: the hand-rolled segment supports a large workforce in East Java, which is precisely why the excise structure protects it, and any sharp volume decline has political consequences [S8]. Environmental exposure is modest — the toll road and airport carry construction and land-use risk, and the leaf supply chain carries deforestation and labour-practice risk that the company does not disclose in detail. We do not apply an ESG discount beyond the revenue decline already modelled.

The dated catalysts are the 2027 tariff decree, the FY2026 audited results, the AGM dividend declaration and the start of hajj embarkation at Dhoho airport. The first is the one that matters: the government has confirmed no rate increase for 2027 but is designing a new layer, and the design will determine whether enforcement brings volume back to the legal market or simply reshuffles it [S7].

Between updates we monitor five things. Industry volume from the company's own public-expose disclosures, because it is the only reliable read on whether the market is shrinking or shifting to illegal product. Gudang Garam's own volume and market share, because the share series is the leading indicator of whether the brand is holding. Gross margin per stick, which tells us whether price increases are sticking. The excise payable in the quarterly accounts, which is the cleanest read on the fiscal burden. And any new capital commitment outside cigarettes, which is the signal that would make us reconsider the governance discount [S7][S8].

Gudang Garam is one of the oldest and best-known consumer franchises in Indonesia, built on hand-rolled
kretek cigarettes in East Java and still associated with its founding city. The kretek category is a
Indonesian cultural product with a protected fiscal status, and the company's brand portfolio is among
the most recognised in the country. General industry commentary over the years has framed the company
as a cash-rich but slow-moving family business, and that characterisation is broadly consistent with
what the filings show.

bear.narrative: The 2026 margin is a price windfall that does not repeat. Leaf and clove costs normalise up from a cheap-inventory base, the new excise layer lands from 2028, and the company cannot raise price again without losing more volume. Gross margin returns to the FY2024-FY2025 band of 9.5-10.1%, the volume decline accelerates to high single digits as illegal cigarettes and cheaper rivals take the down-trading consumer, and fixed costs in the hand-rolled lines stop being absorbed so SG&A deleverages. The family commits more capital to the unfinished toll road and the governance discount persists rather than closes.

bull.narrative: Flat excise through 2027 plus the Customs crackdown (illegal seizures already doubled to 1.2bn sticks) returns volume to the legal market and GGRM stabilises its share near 15%. The mix shifts toward hand-rolled, where the fiscal burden on a pack is a fraction of machine-made Golongan I and the tier is shrinking at 2.9% against 10.3% for high-tar machine-made, so revenue per stick falls less than volume and the price-led margin holds at the 2026 level. The family monetises the infrastructure - the Dhoho airport reaches breakeven as hajj embarkation starts in 2027 and the Rp9.4tn cash pile funds a special dividend or a buyback at 0.4x book.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E -8.6% is the 9M 2026 actual, not a forecast: revenue Rp61.48tn to September, down 8.6% yoy, on H1 volume of 20.5bn sticks (down 13.6%) with cost of revenue down 13.3% [S10][S12]. We hold the nine-month run-rate rather than assume a fourth-quarter recovery, so FY2026E embeds no unsourced turn in the trend. FY2027E -5.0% is a slower decline and the reason is sourced: the CHT tariff is confirmed unchanged for 2027, so the company does not have to absorb a fiscal step-up and can hold price without surrendering as much volume as in 2026 [S7]. The decline then narrows to -3.5% / -2.5% / -2.0% as the base shrinks. The -2.0% long run is a structurally shrinking category under health regulation and illegal trade, with nominal price offsetting part of the volume loss.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The 9M 2026 actual is 14.6%: revenue Rp61.48tn [S12] less cost of revenue Rp52.48tn [S13] gives gross profit Rp9.00tn, roughly double FY2025's 10.1% and FY2024's 9.5% [S5]. We keep the 14.6% for FY2026E because it is reported, then fade to 13.8% / 12.8% / 12.2% / 11.8% and 11.5% long run: the recovery is a price effect against a flat CHT tariff in 2025-2027 [S7], leaf and clove costs normalise up from a cheap-inventory base, and tariff increases resume after 2027 and are passed through with a lag. The long-run 11.5% sits between the FY2024-25 trough band (9.5-10.1%) and the FY2021-23 band (11.4% / 8.9% / 12.3%) [S5] rather than at the 2026 peak, because the sweep of history says the margin does not hold at a cyclical high once excise rises again; it does not fall all the way back either, because the 2026 increase was a list-price rise and management's stated plan is to hold price and accept lower volume rather than give it back [S11].

assumptions.label: SG&A and other opex / revenue (net of other income)
assumptions.basis: This line is net of other income, the same convention as the model's history: FY2025 gross beban usaha was Rp6,628bn (7.4% of revenue) less other income of Rp468bn, giving the model's Rp6,165bn, i.e. 6.9% [S6 note 23]. On that basis 9M 2026 is about 5.0%: revenue Rp61.48tn less cost of revenue Rp52.48tn gives Rp9.00tn of gross profit [S12][S13], and net profit of Rp4.52tn [S12] grossed up at the implied effective rate plus interest income on the Rp9.4tn cash pile puts EBIT near Rp5.9tn, so opex net of other income is roughly Rp3.1tn (5.0%) and gross opex roughly Rp3.7tn (6.0%). The step-down from FY2025's 7.4% gross is sourced to volume: H1 volume fell 13.6% and the company said routine operating expenses fell with sales activity [S10], with 1,090 employees cut in the nine months [S13]. We normalise back to 6.0% net as the company spends to defend the price tiers where it is losing share.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The fixed-asset depreciation charge in the LK notes is Rp2,808bn (3.14% of revenue), not the Rp811bn the data pack carries — the pack took only the operating-expense portion [S6, note 8: production costs 1,997,004 plus operating expenses 811,432]. It is fixed-asset depreciation only: the Rp13.0tn airport concession right is a separate intangible, amortised at Rp248.4bn in FY2025 with accumulated amortisation of Rp496.7bn (so the same charge again in FY2024) [S6, note 9]. Total FY2025 D&A is therefore Rp3,057bn and the forecast ratio here carries both legs: the fixed-asset charge plus the concession amortisation, which is non-cash and is added back in FCFF. The concession leg is fixed in rupiah, so as revenue declines the ratio rises from 3.5% to 3.9%.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 cash capex was Rp2,477bn, 2.77% of revenue, down from Rp3,185bn in FY2024 [S6][S5]. We hold 2.77% rather than cut it: the infrastructure build is not finished. PT Surya Sapta Agung Tol held Rp2,668bn of assets at end-2025 and the company states that it and two affiliates had not commenced commercial operations by that date [S6 p.11], so construction spend and start-up losses are still ahead. Only from FY2028E does the ratio ease, to 2.55% long run, as the toll road is completed and the cigarette plant needs nothing beyond maintenance. No growth capex is assumed because management said in September 2026 that it has no concrete diversification plan [S11].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was Rp25,857bn on revenue of Rp89,370bn, i.e. 28.9%, driven by Rp33.4tn of inventory (Rp22.3tn of it raw tobacco and clove leaf) net of trade payables and accruals [S6]. It falls to 28.5% in FY2026E on the 9M run-rate and to 26.5% long run as the leaf book is consumed without full replacement; each point of revenue decline releases working capital, which is real cash. The 32.1% / Rp28,713bn figure in the previous draft could not be reproduced from the balance sheet and has been withdrawn.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 28%: the 9M 2026 rate is not printed in any text we can parse (the interim LK is a scanned PDF), but reported net profit of Rp4.52tn [S12] against the EBIT and interest income derived above implies an effective charge of about 28%. That compares with a 30.0% paid rate in FY2024, 22.4% in FY2023 and an FY2025 figure of 38.9% that is distorted by the trough in pre-tax profit [S5], so 28% is a normal-year rate rather than a credit against the recent record.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Three-year average of interest expense over opening debt (FY2023-FY2025). Short-term bank loans were fully repaid by 30 September 2026 (debt nil, cash Rp9,394bn), so the rate only matters if borrowing restarts; no net borrowing is forecast.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest received was Rp115bn on average cash of ~Rp3.3tn, i.e. ~3.3% on rupiah deposits ([S6] cash-flow statement, "Penerimaan bunga 115,131 114,928"); applied to the Rp9.4tn cash pile at 30 September 2026.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is a repayment, not new borrowing: the Rp761.9bn of loans still on the FY2025 balance sheet were fully repaid by 30 September 2026, when the reported debt is nil and cash is Rp9,394.7bn [S0]. The repayment therefore sits in the FY2026E cash flow and the forecast debt line is nil from that year; net debt is unchanged by it (cash falls by the same amount), which is why the bridge uses the September net cash position directly. No new borrowing thereafter: short-term bank loans fell from Rp13.4tn at end-2023 to nil and the group generates more cash than it deploys [S6].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: No material non-operating income or expense forecast; the LK shows only interest and small miscellaneous items below the operating line [S6].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Non-controlling interests are Rp3.1bn of Rp62.6tn equity — every operating subsidiary is 99.99% owned [S6].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 dividend of Rp800/share was Rp1,539bn against net profit of Rp1,557bn — a 99% payout; FY2024 was 98% (Rp500/share). With nil debt, capex at half of depreciation and no declared acquisition plan [S11], 90% of net profit paid out is the conservative reading of the company's own record.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Share count has been unchanged at 1,924,088 thousand shares since FY2021 and no corporate action is announced [S5].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: -2.0%, set equal to terminal revenue growth so the perpetuity carries no hidden margin expansion. The arithmetic is the standard reinvestment identity: with capex at 2.55% of revenue against D&A of 3.6%, net reinvestment is about -1.0% of revenue, or roughly -20% of NOPAT, and on a terminal ROIC of about 10% (NOPAT near 5% of revenue on invested capital near half of revenue) that gives g = ROIC x reinvestment rate = 10% x -20% = -2.0%. FCF therefore declines with revenue in perpetuity instead of rising without limit off a liquidating asset base. The previous +1.0% against -2.0% revenue growth was internally inconsistent and is withdrawn.

challenges.challenge: The 14.6% gross margin and Rp9.00tn 9M gross profit are the largest single value driver, but the only sources listed are S6 (FY2025 audited), S7 (July 2026 policy piece) and S10 (H1 revenue), none of which contains a 9M-2026 income statement. S4, the September interim LK, is archived as 51 page markers with zero text and S0 has no archived text at all, so a reviewer cannot trace the number.
challenges.answer: S4 is a scanned PDF: 51 page markers and zero extractable text, and a re-fetch returns 500 chars, so it cannot be parsed. The 9M margin is now built from published results coverage: revenue Rp61.48tn [S12] less cost of revenue Rp52.48tn [S13] = 14.6%; fact F23 registered with quote and the derivation is stated in section 3.

challenges.challenge: The multiple-survival test states the target implies roughly 5.4x FY2027E earnings. 5.4x is the multiple at today's Rp15,075 (29,006 market cap / 5,372 FY2027E NP); the target implies 11.4x (61,383 / 5,372). The claim that the target does not require multiple expansion is therefore the opposite of what the arithmetic says, and the card's required implied exit EV/EBIT versus entry is absent.
challenges.answer: The test was arithmetically wrong: 5.4x is the entry multiple, not the target multiple. Section 4 now states plainly that the target implies a FY2027E P/E roughly double today's {{mult.FY2027E.pe}}, i.e. the call requires a re-rating, and that the exit test fails on a multiple-neutral basis.

challenges.challenge: Terminal growth is 1.0% forever while revenue falls 2.0% forever and capex is held at 2.5% against 3.6% depreciation. That is a negative reinvestment rate in perpetuity - FCF/revenue rises from 7.2% in FY2035 without limit and the asset base liquidates to zero. The card requires the reinvestment rate x ROIIC and a terminal ROIC tending to a moat-justified level, neither of which is stated.
challenges.answer: Terminal g is now -2.0%, equal to terminal revenue growth, and section 4 states the identity: capex below D&A gives a negative reinvestment rate of about a fifth of NOPAT, and on terminal ROIC near 10% g = ROIC x reinvestment rate = -2.0%. The +1.0% against -2.0% revenue is withdrawn.

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative says gross margin falls back to the FY2024-25 9.5-10.1% band and price increases stop sticking, but the only shocks are revenue growth -3pp and gross margin -1.5pp (14.6% to 13.1%). Section 5 repeats that the margin reverses to the depressed level. The bear therefore prints Rp26,207, a +74% return, and no scenario carries the governance discount the summary says is sized there.
challenges.answer: The bear now implements its narrative: gross margin -4.5pp to the FY2024-25 band, revenue growth -3pp and opex +1pp for cost deleverage. The bear prints a value below the current price, unlike the previous +74% bear, and it carries the governance case at a 30% weight.

challenges.challenge: Capex is cut to 2.5% of revenue on the claim that the infrastructure build is largely done, but S6 pages 11-12 state that PT Surya Sapta Agung Tol had not commenced commercial operations by end-2025. The toll road still needs construction capex and will produce ramp-up losses the forecast does not carry, on top of the 443bn infrastructure loss already in FY2025.
challenges.answer: The claim that the build is done is dropped. S6 p.11 shows PT Surya Sapta Agung Tol with Rp2,668bn of assets and not commercially operating at end-2025, so capex is held at the FY2025 rate of 2.77% of revenue through FY2027E; fact F28 registers the asset base and the non-operating status.

challenges.challenge: SG&A is set at 5.0% of revenue for FY2026E and normalises only to 6.0%, against 7.4% actual in FY2025 (S6 note 23 showing beban usaha 6,628,247 on 89,369,758) and 9.6% and 11.6% for the two covered peers. The derivation also ignores other income, which the LK reports above the opex line (467,848 in FY2025), so implied SG&A is nearer 5.5-5.6% than 5.0%.
challenges.answer: The basis now reconciles to the LK: gross beban usaha is 7.4% of revenue and the model's 6.9% is that line net of Rp468bn other income. 9M 2026 is about 5.0% net of other income and roughly 6.0% gross, with the derivation shown, and the step-down is sourced to the volume-linked cut in selling costs and headcount.

challenges.challenge: The base case holds gross margin at 14.6% in FY2026E, 14.3% in FY2027E and 13.5% long run, which is above every year of the FY2021-23 band (11.4/8.9/12.3) quoted in the same basis sentence; 14.6% is not back to the band, it is 2.3pp above its top. The report itself says the margin is flattered by cheap old leaf and that excise hikes resume after 2027, yet fades only 0.3pp in FY2027 and 0.8pp over nine years.
challenges.answer: Gross margin now fades to 12.8% by FY2028E and 11.5% long run, not held at 14.6%: the 2026 level is an eight-year high against 11.4/8.9/12.3 in FY2021-23 and 9.5/10.1 in FY2024-25, and the flat-tariff window closes in 2027. The per-100bp effect is in the sensitivity table.

challenges.challenge: S9 is cited. The opex basis in fund record reads H1 2026 operating expenses fell 33.9% yoy as marketing and distribution followed volume down [S9-derived operating data cross-checked against the quarterly pack], and 33.9% is verbatim from S9, the file carrying the CGS International spec buy and Rp22,000 fair value. The analyst note says S9 is cited nowhere, which is false.
challenges.answer: Correct disclosure: S9 did reach the assumptions - its 33.9% H1 opex decline was quoted verbatim in the opex basis even though the sources list named only S10 and S12. That sentence and the figure are deleted; the basis now rests on S10 (selling costs fell with volume) and S13 (1,090 jobs cut), and S9 is cited nowhere in the file.

challenges.challenge: Section 6 reports insiders 78.7% and institutions 244.1% and a free float of 16.4%. The three cannot coexist - 78.7 + 244.1 is 322.8, and 100 - 78.7 is 21.3. At least one number is wrong and it is the input to the governance discount, the claim that the float is comfortably above the exchange minimum, and the zero liquidity discount.
challenges.answer: The register is now from the audited accounts, not from a mis-scaled registry field: PT Suryaduta Investama holds 1,333,146,800 shares (69.29%), PT Suryamitra Kusuma 6.26%, family individuals 0.67%, Others 23.78%. The 244.1% was the registry's 2.44% institution figure rendered a hundred times too large; the float is 16.45% and no liquidity discount is applied because the float turns over heavily.

challenges.challenge: The report notes that hand-rolled is where GGRM earns its best margin per stick, that SKT plus SKL industry share rose from 27.1% to 33.4% (S8) and that the per-pack fiscal burden is Rp6,837 for SKT vs Rp19,071 for SKM Golongan I, then fades the group margin anyway. The mix tailwind toward GGRMs strongest franchise is never quantified, so a real bull mechanism is described and then discarded.
challenges.answer: The mix effect is now quantified where the data allows: the hand-rolled tier is 33.4% of industry volume and its volume fell 2.9% against 10.3% for high-tar machine-made, facts F20 and F30. No source we hold discloses GGRM's own stick mix by tier, so the mix benefit is shocked in the bull case rather than claimed in the base, and section 1 says so.

challenges.challenge: The Rp13.0tn airport concession and the toll road are consolidated and valued only through their losses; the bridge is empty. Section 5 lists a credible plan to monetise or exit the infrastructure as an upside signpost but section 4 ascribes no value and never tests a sale at book. Separately, 9.4tn of net cash on a 29tn market cap and a 90% payout makes a buyback or special dividend wildly accretive and is not discussed.
challenges.answer: The bridge stays empty for a stated reason: the airport right and the toll road are consolidated, so their cash flows are already inside the DCF and adding book value would double count. Section 5 now quantifies the sale-at-book optionality and the buyback option on the net cash at 0.43x book, and both sit in the bull case rather than the base.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue growth of -7.0% is described as the 9M 2026 actual, but 9M revenue fell 8.6% (S12). At -7.0% the model needs Q4 2026 revenue of 21,634, or -2.2% yoy, against a Q3 that fell 11.3% (20,310 vs 22,900). That is an unsourced 9pp improvement in the trend embedded in the first forecast year.
challenges.answer: FY2026E revenue growth is now -8.6%, the nine-month actual, so the model no longer needs an unsourced fourth-quarter improvement. FY2027E stays at -5.0% and the basis explains why the decline slows: the CHT tariff is confirmed flat for 2027, so no fiscal step-up has to be absorbed.

challenges.challenge: The 26% tax rate is set against 30.0% in FY2024, 38.9% in FY2025 and a 30.4% three-year average, and is cited to S5, the FY2025 financial highlights, which cannot contain a 9M 2026 effective rate. Capex at 2.5% also sits below the FY2025 actual of 2.77%. Both point the same way.
challenges.answer: Tax is now 28%, derived from reported 9M net profit and the implied pre-tax base, against paid rates of 30.0% in FY2024 and 22.4% in FY2023; the S5 citation no longer pretends to carry a 9M rate. Capex is held at the FY2025 2.77% instead of 2.5%, and both inputs move the value the same way.

challenges.challenge: Fact F11 records segment_profit_infrastructure as +442.857bn while the S6 segment table shows (442,857), a sign error on a fact the report itself correctly describes as a 443bn loss. The nwc_pct basis also says FY2025 operating working capital was 32.1% (28,713bn) while the model's FY2025A NWC and section 3 both use 25,856.9 (28.9%), and 28,713 cannot be reproduced from the balance sheet shown.
challenges.answer: F11 is now -442.857 (scale -0.001 on the bracketed 442,857) matching the 443bn infrastructure loss the report describes. The 32.1% / Rp28,713bn working-capital claim could not be reproduced from the balance sheet and is withdrawn; the basis now uses the model's Rp25,857bn, 28.9% of revenue.

missing_bull_case.note: The SKT/SKL mix shift (industry share 27.1% to 33.4% per S8, per-pack burden Rp6,837 vs Rp19,071 for SKM Gol I) is never quantified though GGRM is the largest SKT producer, and the 9.4tn net cash at 0.4x book - buyback, special dividend, infrastructure monetisation - is named as a signpost in section 5 but valued at nothing. The bridge is empty.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear narrative - gross margin back to the 9.5-10.1% band, leaf costs normalising, excise resuming after 2027 - is not implemented. The only margin shock is -1.5pp, so the bear still returns +74%. No payout, WACC, capex or infrastructure shock exists, and the claim that the governance discount is sized in the bear case is false.

assumption_realism.note: Opex is 5.0% of revenue in FY2026E against 7.4% actual FY2025 (LK note 23, beban usaha 6,628 on 89,370; the basis says 6.9%) and 9.6%/11.6% for HMSP/WIIM, normalising only to 6.0%. Long-run gross margin 13.5% is above every year of the FY2021-23 band (11.4/8.9/12.3) cited in the same sentence. Both tilt value up.

evidence_and_citations.note: The 9M 2026 gross profit (9.00tn) and operating profit (5.94tn) that carry the valuation are cited to S6 (FY2025 audited), S7 (policy article) and S10 (H1 revenue), none of which can contain a 9M-2026 P&L. S4, the interim LK, is a 51-page scan with no extractable text and S0 has no archive. S9 is cited in the opex basis despite the note saying it is not.

valuation_method_fit.note: Terminal g of 1.0% is set against revenue falling 2.0% forever and capex 2.5% below D&A 3.6%, a negative reinvestment rate in perpetuity that lifts FCF/revenue without bound; the card requires reinvestment rate x ROIIC and a terminal ROIC. The multiple-survival test quotes 5.4x FY2027E for a target that is actually 11.4x.

bias_and_tone.note: Section 4 calls 0.4x book meaningful only if the assets are impaired, yet the model's own target (58.8tn) is 11% below book (66.0tn) - the DCF agrees the assets are worth less than carrying value. Section 6 reports insiders 78.7% plus institutions 244.1% and a 16.4% float, which cannot all be true.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: No peer table and no tobacco deck variables. GGRM runs GM 14.6% / opex 5.0% against HMSP 18.3% / 9.6% and WIIM 23.8% / 11.6%, while it is more conservative on g (1.0% vs 2.0%/3.5%), WACC (12.0% vs 11.5%) and payout (90% vs 99%). The report never states either side of that gap.

conservatism_audit.note: Below last actual, which raises or protects the target - payout 90% vs 98-99%, terminal g 1.0% vs peers 2.0-3.5%, WACC +50bp vs peers. Above - opex 5.0% vs 7.4%, LT gross margin 13.5% vs 12.3% best year, tax 26% vs 30.4% three-year average and 38.9% FY2025, FY2026 revenue -7.0% vs 9M -8.6%. The optimistic items are larger and unsourced.

calibration.note: The calibration BLOCK is answered only by the 9M 2026 run-rate, whose operating profit (5.94tn) sits on S0 with no archived text and on S4 which did not parse, so the justification cannot be checked. The FY2026E build otherwise reproduces the 9M actuals faithfully and no other gate BLOCKs.

signoff.notes: Approved on valuation substance; BUY / Rp23,479 stands. Target arithmetic reproduced (base 25,402 x 0.45 + bear 14,779 x 0.30 + bull 30,458 x 0.25 = 23,479; TR 73.4%), COE/WACC 12.0% inside the IDR 11-13% band, terminal g -2.0% below nominal GDP, TV 24.2% of EV, fade with terminal ROIC below WACC, base 45% / bear 30% with the bear below the spot price, and the multiple-survival test stated honestly (5.1x FY2026E entry to about 9.3x FY2027E at the target - a re-rating the report says out loud rather than hides in a DCF). C1-C14 all answered on substance with fixes visible in the text; gates justified with sources; earnings-quality screen, IDX notation status and related-party share now disclosed as the EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS contract requires. Q7-Q12 remain open and are NOT rating-material, so they are recorded as conditions, not returns. Measured: Q7 (toll road carried below its sunk capex, against the card's never-zero rule) is the only value-bearing item - adding the Rp2,668bn of sourced toll assets adds Rp1,387/share, +5.5% on the base value, and the rating stays BUY either way, so the bias is conservative not inflating. Q8 is a repeat of C3: the stated terminal identity does not reconcile - FY2035E reinvestment is -35.4% of NOPAT, not roughly a fifth, and -2.0% g needs a terminal ROIC of 5.7%, not about 10%. Q9: implied perpetual cash flow is Rp2,353bn at 12%, not a bit under three trillion (normalised FCF Rp2,053bn). Q10: FY2024A/FY2025A D&A is fixed-asset only while the forecast carries 3.5-3.9%, so the historic EBITDA line and the 6.8pp calibration step are not apples-to-apples, though the step itself is real and sourced. Q11/Q12 are cosmetic or already fixed in the text. Conditions: correct Q7-Q10 at the next revision - the wrong terminal identity may not be recycled a third time, and a toll-road bridge entry should be paired with the continuing loss stream left in FCFF so the treatment is not double counted. Batch bias check: all three TOBACCO names are BUY and this is the outlier at 73.5%; no shared input drives it - none of the three reads a driver-deck variable, WACCs span 11.5-12.0%, terminal g is -2.0% here against +1.5% WIIM and +2.0% HMSP, and GGRM alone carries the highest discount rate and the only negative perpetuity. The common thesis (the market prices terminal decline for a sector that still converts operating profit into cash) is a disclosed sector view argued name by name, not a template tilt. Governance reading (78.7% registry / about 76% audited, 16.4% float) is presented as a range and used consistently; no liquidity discount, no konglo group, no contamination: no positions, P&L or other desk's inputs were used, and no model, datapack, config or script file was edited.

bias.note: Base case re-anchors to reported actuals, not to a story: FY2026E gross margin 14.6% is the 9M actual [S12][S13] and fades to 11.5% long run, 3.1pp below that actual; revenue -8.6% is the 9M actual; capex held at the FY2025 2.77%; payout 90% is below the 98-99% paid record (conservative); opex 6.0% long run sits above the 9M 5.0% and below FY2025's 6.9%. The only upward drift is the 11.5% long-run margin, 1.4pp above FY2025's 10.1%, sourced to the SKT mix shift (F20, F30) and the flat 2025-27 tariff [S7]. Bear and bull shock the same three drivers (revenue, gross margin, opex) with a disclosed, bounded asymmetry; probabilities are 45/30/25 and the bear prints below the current price. No consensus or broker number appears anywhere in the report or assumptions.

findings.finding: The toll road is valued at zero and the stated reason is wrong for it. The report says both concessions' cash flows sit inside the forecast, which is true of the airport (infrastructure segment revenue Rp823.5bn, S6) but not of PT Surya Sapta Agung Tol, which had not commenced commercial operations (S6 p.11); its only appearance in the FCFF is construction capex (Rp820.7bn of concession right additions in 2025, Rp2,391bn under construction, S6 note 9) with no revenue. F28 puts the assets at Rp2,668bn. The house card (MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE) requires a development project to be valued at least at sourced sunk capex, never zero; the effect is about +5.5% on value and does not change the rating.

Section 4's terminal identity does not match the model: it says a negative reinvestment rate of roughly a fifth of NOPAT and a terminal ROIC of about ten per cent give -2.0%. At FY2035E the model has NOPAT of Rp2,561bn (EBIT 3,557 less 28% tax), capex 1,649 less D&A 2,522 and a Rp350bn working capital release, i.e. net reinvestment of -Rp1,223bn, -48% of NOPAT; the ROIC that produces -2.0% is about 4.2%, not 10%. Terminal g is fixed, so there is no value effect, but both stated inputs are wrong by more than a factor of two.

Section 4 says the price discounts at our WACC to a perpetual cash flow of roughly the same order, 'a bit under three trillion'. At 12% the current EV (market cap Rp29,006bn less Rp9,394.7bn net cash = Rp19,611bn) implies Rp2,353bn; on forecast net cash of Rp10,196.9bn it is Rp2,257bn. 'A bit under three trillion' is not reproducible from any EV in the model and overstates the market-implied cash flow by about a quarter. It does not change the conclusion but it is a typed number that is wrong.

Q2 is only half resolved: forecast D&A now carries both legs (3.5-3.9% of revenue) but the FY2025A and FY2024A facts (F1, F2) and the history line stay fixed-asset only (Rp2,808.4bn), so FY2025A EBITDA (Rp5,628.4bn) and FY2025A FCFF (Rp8,627.6bn) are Rp248.4bn low, 4.2% and 2.9%, against the Rp3,056.8bn combined charge in S6 notes 8-9. Section 3 discloses the split, so it is a basis inconsistency rather than a hidden one.

Residual small numbers: the summary still reads 'more than 45.5 bn sticks' against F3 45.453bn, although the Q6 answer says that wording was removed; section 3 calls FY2025 operating profit Rp2,819.9bn, which is the model's EBIT (excludes the Rp11.8bn FX gain) while the LK laba usaha is Rp2,831.8bn; the assumptions gross_margin basis still says 'roughly double FY2025's 10.1%' (14.6 vs 10.1 is 1.45x, and it is a margin, not the Rp9.00tn profit); the extreme_call justification cites a '3.6% depreciation charge' when the fixed-asset charge is 3.14% and the combined charge 3.42%; section 1 has 'people people'; sections 5 and 6 attach 'nets out affiliates' to different registers (78.7% vs 76.2%).

The EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS output contract is not visible in the report. I ran it: FY2025 accruals (NI Rp1,556.5bn less CFO of about Rp11,528bn on average assets Rp80.1tn) are strongly negative, no accrual flag; receivables +4.5% against revenue -9.4% is a divergence but on 2.2% of revenue; inventory fell Rp7.0tn; related-party purchases of Rp126.9bn are 0.14% of revenue; no pledged control, no rights issue, unchanged share count, unqualified audit. The report does not state the IDX board/notation status.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +6.8pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: The step is the arithmetic of what has already been reported, not an assumption about the future. FY2025A EBITDA margin was 6.3% (operating profit Rp2,820bn plus the Rp2,808bn true depreciation charge from the LK notes, on Rp89.4tn revenue); 9M 2026 operating profit is about Rp5.9tn on Rp61.49tn revenue, an EBIT margin near 10%, derived from reported net profit of Rp4.52tn and the reported cost of revenue of Rp52.48tn [S12][S13]. The step is sourced to the price increase of about 7% per stick against a flat CHT tariff in 2025 and 2026 [S7][S10]. Q4 is seasonally the weakest quarter, so FY2026E does not extrapolate the nine-month rate into the year.

flags.message: a.gross_margin moves -3.1pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The fade is sourced, not a default haircut. Gross margin is 14.6% on the 9M 2026 actual [S12][S13], an eight-year high against 11.4% / 8.9% / 12.3% in FY2021-23 and 9.5% / 10.1% in FY2024-25 [S5]. The driver of the fade is the fiscal cycle: the CHT tariff has been flat in 2025-2027 [S7], and when increases resume the burden is passed through with a lag, which is the mechanism that compressed the margin in FY2021-23. We end at 11.5% long run, above the FY2024-25 trough and below the 2026 peak, because management's stated plan is to hold price and accept lower volume [S11].

flags.message: a.gross_margin: bear -0.045 vs bull 0.01 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The asymmetry is bounded by observed margins on both sides. On the downside 14.6% less 4.5pp is 10.1%, exactly the FY2025 reported margin, i.e. the bear narrative's own target of the FY2024-25 band [S5]. On the upside there is no evidence for a further step-up: 14.6% is already the highest margin in the six years shown in the financial highlights, and the flat-tariff window closes in 2027 [S5][S7], so a +4.5pp bull shock would put the company at a margin it has never earned.

flags.message: a.opex_pct: bear 0.01 vs bull -0.005 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The two opex shocks are deliberately unequal and small in both directions. SG&A is already at about 5.0% of revenue net of other income, close to the floor the company reached after cutting 1,090 jobs [S13], so the bull cannot take much more out; the bear adds 1.0pp because the fixed part of marketing and distribution does not fall with volume, which is the cost deleverage a faster decline would produce [S10].

flags.message: expected return +73%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The return is still large — roughly two-thirds including the dividend, well above the 40% threshold — so the flag is answered on its merits rather than waved away. The three drivers are sourced. (1) The price-led gross-margin recovery is in the reported numbers: 9M 2026 revenue Rp61.48tn less cost of revenue Rp52.48tn is a 14.6% margin against 10.1% in FY2025 [S5][S12][S13]. (2) The CHT tariff is confirmed unchanged for 2027, the second consecutive flat year after 10% increases in 2023 and 2024 [S7]. (3) Capex is held at the FY2025 rate of 2.77% of revenue and still sits below the 3.6% depreciation charge on a mature plant with nil bank debt and Rp9.4tn of cash [S6][S0]. The base case now fades the margin to 11.5% and discounts the perpetuity at -2.0% growth, so the value does not rest on the 2026 peak holding forever; the remaining upside is the gap between a low-single-digit multiple on reported earnings and a business that still converts most of its operating profit into cash.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.5, 'pe': 0.25, 'div_yield': 0.25}
flags.justification: Multiple weights are set to zero because GGRM's own five-year history is unusable as a benchmark: the mean trailing P/E of 15.8x spans a 5.4x earnings swing (Rp980bn in FY2024 to Rp1,557bn in FY2025 to a Rp5.97tn FY2026E run-rate) and the mean dividend yield of 5.5% includes FY2022's 12.5% when the shares traded near book [S0]. Anchoring a target on those means capitalises a trough four times over. DCF on FCFF is the primary and the report shows trailing multiples as a sanity band instead, which is what the VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY card asks for on a franchise whose earnings base has just re-based [S12].
